scenes.headline: How schemas steer a 14 MB tool-calling model
scenes.sub: Cactus's needle-environments: six product surfaces, five tools each, 32 test cases.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Grape! Needle environments are six Python files for fine-tuning Cactus's fourteen-megabyte tool caller. Here's how they work.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: On a small model with a byte-level grammar, your schema is part of the decoder: bounds, enum names and missing fields shape every token.
scenes.mark: your schema is part of the decoder
scenes.say: The idea: on a small model with a byte-level grammar, the schema is part of the decoder. Bounds, enum names and missing fields shape every token.

steps.say: Each file declares five tools for one product, like a smart home. The engine compiles those schemas into a byte-level grammar.
A request goes to Needle 2, a forty-five-million-parameter model, and the grammar constrains every byte it writes.
It answers with a tool call, or an empty list when no tool fits.

steps.note: pass: 29 of 32, and no critical failures
steps.say: Thirty-two test cases at the bottom of the file check the answers. Twenty-nine passes and no critical failures, and it passes.

scenes.title: Schema rules, learned the hard way

items.text: Delete the field it likes guessing
items.say: Delete optional fields the model tends to guess. The oven takes a temperature, and nothing else.

items.text: Put the bounds in the grammar
items.say: Bounds compile into the grammar, so an oven at four hundred has no representation to emit.

items.text: Keep enum names out of words
items.say: Each enum value is matched against the query text. A room named office grounds the off action, so the demo home has a study.
And five tools each, because the retrieval head shows only the top five per turn.

scenes.label: A model that refuses everything, on one file
scenes.note: the 0.9 is a pass threshold, not a measured score
scenes.say: The ninety percent in the pitch is that gate, not a score. A refuse-everything model fails zero critical cases: they all expect refusals.

scenes.text: Design the schema for the decoder: delete what it guesses, bound what it fills, and name what it matches carefully.
scenes.mark: Design the schema for the decoder
scenes.say: Design the schema for the decoder. Delete what it guesses, bound what it fills, and name what it matches carefully.

recap: Five tools, compiled into a byte-level grammar
No guessable fields, and enum names that can't hide
The 0.9 is a pass gate, not a score
scenes.say: To recap: schemas compiled into the grammar, rules earned the hard way, and a ninety percent that's a gate.
